# 320: Aesthedes C100/0006

A card with six I/O ports and two UARTs.

<!-- $Begin-Autogenerated$ FeaturedPic aes_io -->
[![Aesthedes C100-0006, front](https://www.egueli.com/aesthedes/thumbs/cards/320_AesC100-0006_SN778/IMG_20260220_131401.jpg)](https://www.egueli.com/aesthedes/pics/cards/320_AesC100-0006_SN778/IMG_20260220_131401.jpg)

Aesthedes C100-0006, front


<!-- $End-Autogenerated$ -->

The main chips are:

* 3x HD6821P / HD68421P PIA (Peripheral Interface Adapter) 
* 2x HD6850 / HD68450 ACIA

There are four side connectors:

* Three of them are IDC 13x2 connectors. Each of them breaks out the I/O connection of each PIA (PA0..7, PB0..7, CA1/2, CB1/2).
* The fourth connector is for the two ACIAs.

Between each PIA and its connector, there are two pairs of jumpers in a square pattern. They can connect the four pins horizontally or vertically. They seem to be connected to the CAx/CBx pins.

They are aligned to pins 1, 2, 19 and 20 of the PIA. I'll call them J1, J2, J19 and J20.

## Parallel connector pinout

In the pictures of the PCB component side, pin 1 is at bottom-left. The table below reflects such layout.

| Name | PinL | PinR | Name |
| ---: | ---: | ---- | ---- |
|    ? |   26 | 25   | ?    |
|  X19 |   24 | 23   | X1   |
|  PB0 |   22 | 21   | PB1  |
|  PB2 |   20 | 19   | PB3  |
|  PB4 |   18 | 17   | PB5  |
|  PB6 |   16 | 15   | PB7  |
|    ? |   14 | 13   | ?    |
|  PA7 |   12 | 11   | PA6  |
|  PA5 |   10 | 9    | PA4  |
|  PA3 |    8 | 7    | PA2  |
|  PA1 |    6 | 5    | PA0  |
|   X2 |    4 | 3    | X20  |
|    ? |    2 | 1    | ?    |

Same pinout, in numerical order:

| Pin | Name |
| --: | ---- |
|   1 | ?    |
|   2 | ?    |
|   3 | X20  |
|   4 | X2   |
|   5 | PA0  |
|   6 | PA1  |
|   7 | PA2  |
|   8 | PA3  |
|   9 | PA4  |
|  10 | PA5  |
|  11 | PA6  |
|  12 | PA7  |
|  13 | ?    |
|  14 | ?    |
|  15 | PB7  |
|  16 | PB6  |
|  17 | PB5  |
|  18 | PB4  |
|  19 | PB3  |
|  20 | PB2  |
|  21 | PB1  |
|  22 | PB0  |
|  23 | X1   |
|  24 | X19  |
|  25 | ?    |
|  26 | ?    |

* X20: if J19/J20 are horizontal, this is CA2 else CB1.
* X19: if J19/J20 are horizontal, this is CB1 else CA2.
* X1: if J1/J2 are horizontal, this is CB2 (*) else CA1 (**)
* X2: if J1/J2 are horizontal, this is CA1 else CB2 (*)

(*) Given that the other three jumpers connect to Cxx lines, I deduce that it connects to CB2. I can't tell from the pictures, the trace might be on the top side below the IC.

(**) Given how these jumpers work, I got this by exclusion.

The pinout is rotationally symmetric: it is set up in such a way that it may be reversed to allow Port B to be connected to Port A (and related control lines) and vice versa. In a such a setup, i.e. when pin 1 of the flat cable is on the wrong side on one end, the mapping would be as follows:

| Pin, normal | Name, normal | Name, reversed | Pin, reversed |
| ----------: | -----------: | -------------- | ------------- |
|           1 |            ? | ?              | 26            |
|           2 |            ? | ?              | 25            |
|           3 |          X20 | X19            | 24            |
|           4 |           X2 | X1             | 23            |
|           5 |          PA0 | PB0            | 22            |
|           6 |          PA1 | PB1            | 21            |
|           7 |          PA2 | PB2            | 20            |
|           8 |          PA3 | PB3            | 19            |
|           9 |          PA4 | PB4            | 18            |
|          10 |          PA5 | PB5            | 17            |
|          11 |          PA6 | PB6            | 16            |
|          12 |          PA7 | PB7            | 15            |
|          13 |            ? | ?              | 14            |
|          14 |            ? | ?              | 13            |
|          15 |          PB7 | PA7            | 12            |
|          16 |          PB6 | PA6            | 11            |
|          17 |          PB5 | PA5            | 10            |
|          18 |          PB4 | PA4            | 9             |
|          19 |          PB3 | PA3            | 8             |
|          20 |          PB2 | PA2            | 7             |
|          21 |          PB1 | PA1            | 6             |
|          22 |          PB0 | PA0            | 5             |
|          23 |           X1 | X2             | 4             |
|          24 |          X19 | X20            | 3             |
|          25 |            ? | ?              | 2             |
|          26 |            ? | ?              | 1             |

Do note that in a reverse-mapping setup the X* wires are exchanged, achieving the same effect of switching the J1/J2 and J19/20 jumper pairs. In fact, here's how the control lines would be wired:

| Pin, normal | Name, normal | Name, reversed | Pin, reversed |
| ----------: | -----------: | -------------- | ------------- |
|           3 |          CA2 | CB1            | 24            |
|           4 |          CA1 | CB2            | 23            |
|          23 |          CB2 | CA1            | 4             |
|          24 |          CB1 | CA2            | 3             |
